subjects.title: Expectation of bivariate Probability Distribution and Discrete Probability Distributions

units.title: Mathematical Expectation (Bivariate Random Variable)
units.topics: 1.1 Definition of raw and central moments, moment generating function (m.g.f), cumulant generating function (c.g.f.). 1.2 Theorems on expectations of sum and product of two jointly distributed random variables. 1.3 Conditional expectation. 1.4 Definitions of conditional mean and conditional variance. 1.5 Definition of covariance, coefficient of correlation, independence and uncorrelatedness of two variables. 1.6 Variance of linear combination of variables Var(aX + bY). 1.7 Numerical examples

units.title: Poisson distribution
units.topics: 2.1 Notation: X ~ P(m) Probability mass function (p. m. f.) of the distribution P(X = x) = e^(-m)*m^x / x! ; x = 0,1,2, ... ; m > 0, 0; otherwise 2.2 M. G. F. and C. G. F. Raw and central moments, mean and variance from M.G.F. & C.G.F. Skewness and kurtosis. 2.4 Situations where this distribution is applicable. 2.5 Additive property. 2.6 Conditional distribution of X given (X+Y). 2.7 Numerical examples

units.title: Geometric distribution
units.topics: 3.1 Notation: X ~ G(p), Geometric distribution on support (0, 1, 2, ...,) with p. m. f. p(x) = pq^x . 3.2 Geometric distribution on support (1, 2,. . .) with p. m. f. p(x) = pq^(x-1) . 0 < p < 1, q = 1 - p. 3.3 Situations where this distribution is applicable. 3.4 Distribution function and lack of memory property. 3.5 M. G. F. and C. G. F. Mean and variance from M.G.F. & C.G.F. 3.6 Numerical examples.

units.title: Negative Binomial Distribution
units.topics: 4.1 Probability mass function (p. m. f.) P(X = x) = (x+k-1 C x) p^k q^x ; x = 0, 1, ... ; 0 < p < 1; q = 1 - p; k > 0 Notation X ~ NB(k,p) 4.2 Graphical nature of p.m.f., 4.3 Negative binomial distribution as a waiting time distribution, 4.4 M. G. F. and C. G. F. Mean and variance from M.G.F. & C.G.F. Skewness, kurtosis. 4.5 Additive property. 4.6 Relation between geometric distribution and negative binomial distribution. 4.7 Poisson approximation to negative binomial distribution. Real life situations. 4.8 Numerical problems.

units.title: Multinomial Distribution
units.topics: 5.1 Probability mass function (p.m.f.) P(X = x) = n! / (x1! x2!... xk!) p1^x1 p2^x2... pk^xk Notations: (X1, X2, ..., Xk) ~ MD(n, p1, p2, ..., pk) 5.2 Joint MGF of (X1, X2, ..., Xk). Mean, variance, covariance, total correlation coefficient, variance - covariance matrix from joint MGF. Rank of variance - covariance matrix and its interpretation, 5.3 Additive property. 5.4 Univariate marginal distribution, distribution of Xi + Xj, 5.5 Conditional distribution of Xi given Xj = r (without proof). 5.6 Conditional distribution of Xi given Xi + Xj= r (without proof). 5.7 Numerical problems.

units.title: Continuous Univariate Distributions
units.topics: 1.1 Continuous sample space: Definition, illustrations. Continuous random variable: Definition, probability density function (p. d. f.), cumulative distribution function (c. d. f.), properties of c. d. f. (without proof), probabilities of events related to random variable. 1.2 Expectation of continuous r. v., expectation of function of r. v. E[g(x)], mean, variance, geometric mean, harmonic mean, raw and central moments. 1.3 Moment generating function (MGF): Definition, properties (without proof). Cumulant generating function (CGF): Definition, properties (without proof). 1.4 Mode, partition values: quartiles (Q1, Q2, Q3), deciles, percentiles. 1.5 Probability distribution of function of r. v. Y = g(X ) : using i) Jacobian of transformation for g(.) monotonic function and one-to-one, on to functions, ii) Distribution function for Y = X2, Y = |X|. iii) M.G.F. of g(X)

units.title: Continuous Bivariate Distributions
units.topics: 2.1 Continuous bivariate random vector or variable (X, Y): Joint p. d. f., joint c. d. f, properties (without proof), probabilities of events related to random variables (events in terms of regions bounded by regular curves, circles, straight lines). Marginal and conditional distributions. 2.2 Expectation of r. v. (X, Y), expectation of function of r. v. E[g(X, Y)], joint moments, Cov(X,Y), Corr(X,Y), conditional mean, conditional variance, regression as a conditional expectation. 2.3 Independence of random variables X and Y. 2.4 Theorems on expectation: i) E(X+Y) = E(X) + E(Y) ii) E(XY) = E(X)E(Y) if X and Y are independent. iii) E(aX + bY + c) & Var(aX + bY + c) (statement only proof not expected) 2.5 Moment generating function (MGF): MXY(t1, t2), MGF of marginal distribution of random variables(r.v.s.), properties 2.6 Probability distribution of transformation of bivariate r. v. 2.7 Numerical Examples

units.title: Standard Univariate Continuous Distributions
units.topics: 3.1 Uniform or Rectangular Distribution 3.1.1 Probability density function (p.d.f.) Notation : X ~ U[a, b], 3.1.2 Sketch of p. d. f., c. d. f., mean, variance, symmetry, MGF. 3.1.3 Distributions of (x-a)/(b-a), (b-x)/(b-a), Y = F(X) 3.1.4 Application of the result to model sampling. 3.2 Normal Distribution 3.2.1 Probability density function (p. d. f.) Notation: X ~ N(µ, σ2) 3.2.2 p. d. f. curve, identification of scale and location parameters, properties of probability curve, mean, variance, MGF, CGF, central moments, mode, points of inflexion of probability curve, mean deviation, additive property. 3.2.3 Probability distribution of SNV, aX+b, aX+bY+c 3.2.4 Central limit theorem (CLT) 3.3 Exponential Distribution 3.3.1 Probability density function (p. d. f.) Notation : X ~ E(α) 3.3.2 Nature of density curve, interpretation of α as interarrival rate, lack of memory property 3.4 Numerical Examples

subjects.title: Statistical Computing By Using MS EXCEL-I

units.title: Standard Discrete Probability Distributions
units.topics: 1.1 Poisson distribution-p.m.f., mean, variance, mode, real life situations where it is applicable, statement of additive property, statement of limiting case of B(n, p). 1.2 Geometric distribution -p.m.f., mean, variance, mode, real life situations where it is applicable. Statement of lack of memory property. 1.3 Negative binomial distribution -p.m.f., mean, variance, real life situations where it is applicable. Relation with geometric distribution, concept of waiting time distribution. 1.4 Numerical Examples

units.title: Continuous Univariate Distributions
units.topics: 2.1 Continuous sample space: Definition, illustrations. Continuous random variable: Definition, probability density function (p.d.f.), cumulative distribution function (c.d.f.), properties of c.d.f. (without proof) 2.2 Mathematical expectation, variance, quartiles and quartile deviation. 2.3 Moment generating function (MGF), Cumulant generating function (CGF): Definition, properties (without proof). 2.4 Numerical Examples

units.title: Standard Continuous Probability Distributions
units.topics: 3.1 Uniform distribution - statement of p.d.f., c.d.f., mean, variance, nature of p.d.f. curve 3.2 Normal distribution- statement of p.d.f., c.d.f., mean, variance, median, mode, nature of p.d.f. curve, statement of additive property, skewness. Standard normal distribution 3.3 Exponential distribution- statement of p.d.f., c.d.f., mean, variance, nature of p.d.f. 3.4 Numerical Examples

units.title: Demography
units.topics: 4.1 Vital events, vital statistics, methods of obtaining vital statistics, rates of vital events, sex ratios, dependency ratio. 4.2 Death/Mortality rates: Crude death rate, specific (age, sex etc.) death rate, standardized death rate (direct and indirect), infant mortality rate. 4.3 Fertility/Birth rate: Crude birth rate, general fertility rate, specific (age, sex etc.) fertility rates, total fertility rate. 4.4 Growth/Reproduction rates: Gross reproduction rate, net reproduction rate. (Simple Numerical examples only). 4.5 Interpretations of different rates, uses and applications. 4.6 Numerical Examples

subjects.title: Practical on Probability Distributions and Demography

units.title: Time Series
units.topics: 1.1 Meaning and utility 1.2 Visualization of Time series 1.3 Components of time series 1.4 Additive and multiplicative models 1.5 Methods of estimating trend using moving average method (3,4 and 5 yearly cycle)

units.title: Theory of Attributes
units.topics: 2.1 Attributes: Concept of a Likert scale, classification, notion of manifold classification, dichotomy, class - frequency, order of a class, positive class- frequency, negative class frequency, ultimate class frequency, relationship among different class frequencies (up to two attributes), and dot operator to find the relation between frequencies, fundamental set of class frequencies. 2.2 Consistency of data up to 2 attributes. 2.3 Concepts of independence and association of two attributes. Yule’s coefficient of association (Q), -1 ≤ Q ≤ 1, interpretation.

units.title: Demography
units.topics: 3.1 Vital events, vital statistics, methods of obtaining vital statistics, rates of vital events, sex ratios, dependency ratio. 3.2 Death/Mortality rates: Crude death rate, specific (age, sex etc.) death rate, standardized death rate (direct and indirect), infant mortality rate. 3.3 Fertility/Birth rate: Crude birth rate, general fertility rate, specific (age, sex etc.) fertility rates, total fertility rate. 3.4 Growth/Reproduction rates: Gross reproduction rate, net reproduction rate. (Simple numerical examples only). 3.5 Interpretations of different rates, uses and applications.

units.title: Tabulation
units.topics: 1.1 Raw data, types of characteristics of data (Attribute and variable), Type of variables (Discrete and continuous) 1.2 Construction of frequency distribution table: parts of table, two way and three-way types of tabulations

units.title: Graphical and diagrammatic representation of the data
units.topics: 2.1 Diagrammatic representation of the data: Bar plot, Subdivided, Multiple, Pie chart 2.2 Graphs - Histogram, frequency curve, less than and more than ogive curves

units.title: Measures of Central Tendency
units.topics: 3.1 Requisition of good measure of central tendency 3.2 mean, (definitions, formulae, merits and demerits, examples) 3.3 median (definitions, formulae, merits and demerits, examples) 3.4 mode (definitions, formulae, merits and demerits, examples)

units.title: Measures of Dispersion
units.topics: 4.1 Range, Quartile deviation (definitions, formula, merits and demerits) 4.2 Coefficient of variation (definitions, formula, merits and demerits)

subjects.title: Evolution/ Development of Statistics in India

units.title: Historical Perspective of Statistics in India
units.topics: Data collection system in ancient times, Statistics and Mathematics in ancient Indian poetry, Inferential Statistics and Statistical Economics before and during 4CE (Vishalaksha’s contributions to inference and Kautilya’s Arthashastra), Statistical System during British India, Statistical System in Independent India, Research Teaching and Training in Statistics.

units.title: History and Concept of Probability in ancient India
units.topics: Concept of permutation and combination in ancient India, notations and rule for binomial expansion given by Pingala and others, history of probability – Rug veda, Mahabharata, Indian-Jaina philosophy.

units.title: Contribution of Statisticians in the development of Statistics in India
units.topics: P. C. Mahalanobis, Pandurang Vasudeo Sukhatme, Raghu Raj Bahadur, Debabrata Basu, Gopinath Kallianpur, Keshav Raghavan Nair, Calyampudi Radhakrishna Rao, Vasant Shankar Huzurbazar

units.title: Official Statistics in India
units.topics: Know about Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) of Indian Government, Standing Committee on Statistics (its past and new overhaul. Historical perspective of Official Statistics in India. Overview of present Indian Statistical System: Statistical organizations and their functions – ISI, CSO, NSO.

units.title: Tests of Significance
units.topics: 1.1 Statistics and Parameter, Random sample x1, x2, … , xn from a distribution. Sampling distribution of a statistic, standard error with illustrations. Statistical hypothesis, null and alternative hypothesis, one sided and two sided alternative hypothesis, critical region, type - I and type - II error, level of significance, p-value. Large sample tests: a) test for population mean b) test for equality of two population mean c) test for population proportion d) test for equality of two population proportion e) test for population correlation f) test for equality of two population correlation. 1.2 Two-sided confidence interval for a) population mean b) equality of two population mean c) population proportion d) equality of two population proportion.

units.title: Multiple Linear Regression (Trivariate Case)
units.topics: 2.1 Multiple correlation coefficient. Definition, equation of plane of regression, properties. 2.2 Properties of multiple correlation coefficient. 2.3 Interpretation of coefficient of multiple determination. 2.4 Partial correlation coefficient: Definition and property. 2.5 Notion of multiple linear regression. Yule’s notation (trivariate case). Fitting of regression plane of Y on X1 and X2 by method of least squares. Residual: Definition, order, derivation of variance, properties.

units.title: Time series analysis
units.topics: 3.1 Examples of time series, Objectives of time series, Meaning and utility of time series. 3.2 Components of time series. 3.3 Additive and multiplicative models. 3.4 Meaning of trend, Methods of estimating trend: moving average method, fitting of linear and quadratic trends by least squares method. 3.5 Elimination of trend. 3.6 Meaning of seasonal variations, Methods of estimating seasonal variations: Simple average method, ratio to trend method, ratio to moving average method.

units.title: Gamma Distribution
units.topics: 1.1 Probability density function (p.d.f.) of Gamma distribution with parameter α, λ. Plotting of p.d.f. curve for various parameter values, special cases: i) α = 1, ii) λ = 1 1.2 Mode, cumulative distribution function (c. d. f.), M.G.F. and its use to find mean, variance, moments, cumulants, γ1 and γ2. Additive property, distribution of sum of independent gamma variates. 1.3 Distribution of X/(X+Y) and X/Y where X and Y are independent gamma variates. 1.4 Numerical problems.

units.title: Chi-Square (χ2) Distribution
units.topics: 2.1 Definition of chi-square r. v. as a sum of squares of n i.i.d. standard normal variables. Derivation of the p.d.f. of chi-square with n degrees of freedom (d.f.). 2.2 M.G.F. and C.G.F., Mean, variance, moments, cumulants, mode, skewness and kurtosis. Additive property. 2.3 Distribution of X/(X+Y) and X/Y where X and Y are independent chi-square variates. 2.4 Normal approximation to Chi-square distribution.

units.title: Student’s t-distribution
units.topics: 3.1 Definition of t r.v. with n d.f. 3.2 Derivation of the p.d.f of t distribution. Plotting of p.d.f. curve for various parameter values, mean, variance, moments, mode. Use of t-tables for calculations of probabilities, statement of normal approximation. 3.3 Distinction between density curves of normal and t-distributions.

units.title: Snedecor’s F – distribution
units.topics: 4.1 Definition of F r.v. with n1 and n2 d.f. 4.2 Derivation of the p.d.f, plotting of p.d.f. curve for various parameter values, mean, variance, moments, mode. 4.3 Distribution of 1/F, use of F-tables for calculation of probabilities. Interrelationship between Chi-square, t and F distributions.

units.title: Tests of Hypothesis based on sampling distributions
units.topics: 5.1 Tests based on Chi-square distribution: a) Test for goodness of fit b) Test for independence of two attributes c) Test for population variance. 5.2 Tests based on t-distribution: a) Test for population mean b) Test for equality of two population means c) Paired t-test d) Test for population correlation coefficient. 5.3 Tests based on F-distribution: a) Test for equality of two population variances.

subjects.title: Statistical Computing By Using MS EXCEL-II

units.title: Sampling Distributions
units.topics: 1.1 Chi-Square (χ2) distribution: Statement of p.d.f., mean and variance, applications of the Chi-Square distribution, use of Chi-Square tables for calculations of probabilities. 1.2 Student’s t-distribution: Statement of p.d.f., mean and variance, applications of the t distribution, use of t tables for calculations of probabilities. 1.3 Snedecor’s F distribution: Statement of p.d.f., mean and variance, applications of the F distribution, use of F tables for calculations of probabilities.

units.title: Basic Concepts of Hypothesis Testing and Theory of Estimation
units.topics: 2.1 Population, Sample, Parameter, Statistic, Estimator and Estimate. 2.2 Point estimation and Interval estimation. 2.3 Statistical hypothesis, null and alternative hypotheses, simple and composite hypotheses, one-sided and two-sided alternative hypotheses, critical region, type-I and type-II error, notion of size and power of test, level of significance, p-value. Two-sided confidence interval.

units.title: Tests based on normal distribution
units.topics: 3.1 Test for population means: i) H0 : µ = µ0 against H1: µ ≠ µ0 H1: µ > µ0, H1: µ < µ0, (variance known) ii) H0 : µ1 = µ2 against H1: µ1 ≠ µ2 H1: µ1 > µ2, H1: µ1 < µ2 (variances are known) 3.2 Tests for population proportions: i) H0 : P = P0 against H1: P ≠ P0 H1: P > P0, H1: P < P0, ii) H0 : P1 = P2 against H1: P1 ≠ P2 H1: P1 > P2, H1: P1 < P2.

units.title: Tests based on sampling distributions
units.topics: 4.1 Test for independence of two attributes 4.2 Test for goodness of fit. 4.3 Test for population variance. 4.4 Tests for population means: a) one sample and two sample b) two-sided confidence interval for population mean (variance unknown). 4.5 Paired t-test. 4.6 Test for equalities of two population variances.

subjects.title: Practical on Sampling Distributions and Statistical Inference

units.title: Index Number
units.topics: 1.1 Concept and uses of Index numbers in different fields 1.2 Simple and weighted index numbers 1.3 Cost of living index numbers 1.4 Lasprayes, Paasches and Fisher’s Index numbers

units.title: Concepts and definitions related to testing of hypothesis
units.topics: 3.1 Concept of testing of hypothesis and theory of estimation 3.2 Definitions: population, sample, SRSWR, SRSWOR, random sample from a probability distribution, parameter, statistic. 3.3 Concept of null hypothesis and alternative hypothesis, critical region, level of significance, type I and type II error, one sided and two sided test, degree of freedom, p-value. Large sample tests for mean and proportion (one and two sample tests).

units.title: Designing Questionnaires and Processing Survey Data
units.topics: 3.1 Types of Questions: Open-ended, Close-ended, Likert Scale (5-point, 7-point), Ranking, Multiple Choice. Question design principles: clarity, neutrality, avoiding leading/double-barreled questions. 3.2 Designing online survey forms using digital platforms like Google Forms, Survey Monkey, Form Façade (an add-on to customize Google Forms), etc. 3.3 Processing Survey Data: Downloading responses as MS-Excel sheets, computation of summated scores (for Likert scale-based questions)

units.title: Index Number
units.topics: 1.1 Concept and uses of Index numbers in different fields 1.2 Simple and weighted index numbers 1.3 Cost of living index numbers 1.4 Lasprayes, Paasches and Fisher’s Index numbers

units.title: Concepts and definitions related to testing of hypothesis
units.topics: 2.1 Concept of testing of hypothesis and theory of estimation 2.2 Definitions: population, sample, SRSWR, SRSWOR, random sample from a probability distribution, parameter, statistic. 2.3 Concept of null hypothesis and alternative hypothesis, critical region, level of significance, type I and type II error, one sided and two sided test, degree of freedom, p-value. Large sample tests for mean and proportion (one and two sample tests).

units.title: Time Series
units.topics: 3.1 Introduction, Meaning and utility 3.2 Visualization of Time series 3.3 Components of time series 3.4 Additive and multiplicative models 3.5 Methods of estimating trend using moving average method (3,4 and 5 yearly cycle) 3.6 Numerical problems

units.title: Introduction to R Programming
units.topics: 1.1 Overview of R and R Studio, R syntax, data types (numeric, character, logical). 1.2 Data structures: Vectors, Matrices, Data Frames, and Lists. 1.3 Basic operations: Arithmetic, logical, and relational operators. 1.4 Importing and exporting data (CSV, Excel). 1.5 Data manipulation using subset(), merge(), and transform().

units.title: Data Visualization in R
units.topics: 2.1 Graphical representation: Bar plot, Pie chart, Histogram, Frequency polygon. 2.2 Advanced plots: Scatter plot, Box plot, Density plot. 2.3 Customizing plots: Adding titles, labels, legends, and colors.

units.title: Measures of Central Tendency and Dispersion
units.topics: 3.1 Computing arithmetic mean, geometric mean, harmonic mean, mode and median. 3.2 Partition values: Quartiles, deciles, percentiles. 3.3 Measures of dispersion: Range, quartile deviation, mean deviation, standard deviation, variance, coefficient of variation.
